findings.issue: Audit-report references point to `logs/working/task-9/code-reviewer-*.json`, `task-10/security-auditor-*.json`, `task-11/test-reviewer-*.json`. But Tasks 9/10/11 are audit tasks with `reviewers: []` — they do not produce reviewer JSONs at those paths. Their actual deliverables are audit reports under `logs/audits/` (e.g. Task 11 writes `logs/audits/test-audit.json` per its own AC). The cross-references will not resolve to existing files at QA execution time.
findings.fix: Update Context Files in Task 12 to reference the actual audit-report paths produced by Tasks 9/10/11. Likely: `work/t-hunted-pt-source/logs/audits/code-audit.json`, `logs/audits/security-audit.json`, `logs/audits/test-audit.json`. Align with the path scheme used in Task 11's own AC for `test-audit.json`.

findings.issue: Context Files lists `[logs/deploy/deploy-test.log](../logs/deploy/deploy-test.log)` as a context file, but this artefact is created by this task itself — it does not yet exist when the agent reads context. Including a self-produced deliverable under Context Files is mildly misleading; it belongs under Details → Files (where it is also listed).
findings.fix: Remove the `deploy-test.log` link from Context Files. It is already accurately described under Details → Files as the new artefact this task produces.

findings.issue: `depends_on: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]` lists every Wave 1-3 task. Tech-spec assigns Tasks 9, 10, 11 to the Audit Wave (Wave 4) as parallel siblings, all of which need Wave 1-3 done. The dependency is logically correct, but the list could be simplified by depending on a representative completion gate or by relying on `wave: 4` semantics (waves enforce ordering already in the feature-execution flow). Not a correctness issue, just verbosity that has to be kept in sync with Wave 1-3 task IDs if they ever renumber.
findings.fix: Optional: trim `depends_on` to the latest task(s) of Wave 3 (e.g. [7, 8]) since Wave 3 already transitively depends on Waves 1-2. Or leave as-is for explicitness — both are acceptable.

findings.issue: AC item «Финальный статус в JSON — `passed` (criticals == 0)» is tautological as a criterion — the task's job is to determine pass/fail, not to guarantee a passing outcome. A failing QA is still a valid completion of the task (it just blocks merge). Listing `passed` as an AC mildly conflates outcome with deliverable.
findings.fix: Reword to: «JSON-отчёт содержит детерминированный финальный статус (`passed` или `failed`) согласно правилу `criticals == 0`». The AC then validates that the decision rule was applied, not that QA itself succeeded.

findings.issue: Tech-spec Acceptance Criteria includes `t_hunted_source.py ≤170 LOC` (soft check). Task 12 covers it via `wc -l t_hunted_source.py` in Verification Steps → Smoke (with «>200 LOC → minor» note), but the tech-spec threshold is ≤170 LOC, and Task 12's threshold is 130-170 expected, >200 = minor. The threshold mapping (170 in tech-spec vs >200 minor in Task 12) is slightly looser than tech-spec.
findings.fix: Align the LOC threshold in Task 12 Verification Steps with tech-spec: treat >170 LOC as the soft-check breach (severity = minor per tech-spec soft-check intent). Either tighten the Task 12 threshold or add a comment explaining the looser bound.
